events.description:

Get It Right Music in association with BK One Productions is proud to present our late summer/early fall music documentary and horror film movies (yes, those two things go together, and yes, we ARE wondering why you are asking!). Watch fan favorites on our 16-foot wide LED video wall and enjoy the film in full concert sound!
You have reached the ticketing page for David Bowie – Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars!
Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars (sometimes called Bowie 1973) is a 1979 British documentary/concert film by D. A. Pennebaker. It features English singer-songwriter David Bowie and his backing group the Spiders from Mars performing at the Hammersmith Odeon in London on 3 July 1973, the final date of his Ziggy Stardust Tour. At this show, Bowie made the sudden surprise announcement that the show would be “the last show that we’ll ever do”, later understood to mean that he was retiring his Ziggy Stardust persona.

events.title: David Zayas Jr. Premiere Solo Photography Show
events.description:
DAVID ZAYAS JR.: SOLO ART SHOW
Friday, September 18 at 8PM
Tom Kane Theatre at brooklynONE Productions
brooklynONE Productions presents the first-ever solo photography exhibition from Bronx-born photographer, filmmaker, actor and director David Zayas Jr.
Long before his work as a theatre and film director, Zayas began his artistic journey behind the camera. Over more than a decade, photography became a foundation for a creative career that would eventually take him across New York’s independent film and theatre communities. Now, for the first time, that body of photographic work takes center stage.
DAVID ZAYAS JR.: SOLO ART SHOW transforms the Tom Kane Theatre into a gallery for an evening celebrating Zayas’ photography, visual storytelling and distinctive perspective on the people and world around him.
Zayas is a multidisciplinary New York artist and member of LAByrinth Theater Company and The Actors Studio’s Playwright/Directors Unit. His directing career includes his Off-Broadway debut with Sam Shepard’s Simpatico, work with LAByrinth’s Barn Series, Chain Theatre, Planet Connections and Actors Theatre of NY, as well as brooklynONE Productions, where he has previously directed on the Tom Kane Theatre stage that will now house his first solo photography exhibition. His work also extends into independent filmmaking, with films screened and recognized at festivals around the country.
For bkONE, this exhibition marks another chapter in an ongoing artistic relationship with Zayas, this time turning the spotlight away from the stage and toward the images he creates behind the camera.
Join David, brooklynONE and the NYC arts community for the opening of this landmark first solo exhibition and an evening dedicated to independent art, photography and storytelling.
PLEASE NOTE: This exhibition contains mature content and is intended for guests ages 18 and older.
Friday, September 18 • 8PM
Tom Kane Theatre at brooklynONE Productions
51 35th Street, Building 5
Industry City, Brooklyn

Most recently, she directed the debut comedy special from her and herlongtime comedy partner, Krystyna Hutchinson. The special is set to air in February 2022. The duo is most known for co-creating and co-hosting their groundbreaking, genre-creating GUYS WE F*CKED: The Anti Slut-Shaming podcast — a vulnerable firsthand look into modern female sexuality from a comedic perspective — which began tearing up charts in December 2013. Over eight years later, the show boasts millions of listeners nationally and internationally and has inspired dozens of female-led comedy/sexuality shows. The podcast has hit #1 on the iTunes comedy charts multiple times and has been featured in Vogue, Interview, Esquire, The Huffington Post, The Daily Beast, Splitsider, Mother Jones, Perez Hilton, Elle, A.V. Club, E! News, People, US Magazine, Bust, CNN, and The Village Voice as well as on Sirius Radio, and NBC’s Last Call with Carson Daly. High-profile guests include Amanda Knox, Amber Rose, and Fran Drescher. The podcast was also turned into a book by HarperCollins entitled F*CKED: Being Sexually Explorative and Self-Confident in a World That’s Screwed and the duo was asked to give a TEDx talk exploring topics from their show.Corinne first made a splash in the comedy scene with her debut one-woman show Corinne Fisher: I STALK YOU (Dir. David Crabb) which had a run at The Peoples Improv Theater in the Summer of 2010 and was a featured show in Time Out New York. Since then, she has been a regular on the stand-up scene selling out shows at world-famous clubs like The Comedy Store, New York Comedy Club, The Stand, and Caroline’s on Broadway and theaters such as The Wilbur in Boston, the Athenaeum inChicago, and the Tribeca Performing Arts Center in New York City. Fisher has also been selected to perform at the prestigious Just For Laughs Comedy Festival in both Montreal and Toronto, Moontower Comedy Festival, Boston Comedy Festival, and cult favorite Skankfest. She’s been seen on FOX’s LAUGHS and her show with fellow comic Katie Hannigan THE COMEDIENNE PROJECT (Dir. Ted Alexandro) was selected for the NYC Fringe Festival.Fisher remains an innovator in podcasting, having co-created the WITHOUT A COUNTRY podcast which she currently co-hosts with comedian Shayne Smith, a weekly news shows that covers stories using aslew of sources from various political perspectives. She also previously co-hosted and co-created TWO LESS LONELY GIRLS, a podcast for adult Justin Bieber fans with comedian Rosebud Baker.Right now, Corinne is working on writing and producing several projects including the cartoon series MYSTERY SQUAD GALS created by Ryan Duff. In an unexpected plot twist, she also took over her Dad’sbaseball card and horror collectibles store, Perfectly Centered, in 2021.

events.title: Led Zeppelin Live in Earl’s Court Film Screening with Remastered Audio and Scintillating Video
events.description:
Reduce FOMO! Click here for guaranteed RSVP!
https://wl.eventim.us/event/led-zeppelin-earls-court/704436?afflky=Getitrightthefirsttime
Get It Right Music in association with BK One Productions is proud to present our late summer/early fall music documentary and horror film movies (yes, those two things go together, and yes, we ARE wondering why you are asking!). Watch fan favorites on our 16-foot wide LED video wall and enjoy the film in full concert sound!
You have reached the ticketing page for Led Zeppelin – Earl’s Court!
By 1975, Led Zeppelin were the undisputed heavyweight champions of the rock ’n’ roll universe. That year, all six of the band’s records had re-entered the charts in the wake of the release of Physical Graffiti, and their tour of North America had been one of the most lucrative of all time. They capped off what had already been a banner year with a career-defining five-night residency at London’s Earls Court Exhibition Centre, begun on May 17, 1975.
This is a brand new edit of an entire show from this historic run featuring remastered surround sound and newly remastered video!
Event Info
Film: Led Zeppelin – Earl’s Court
Date: September 24, 2026
Doors: 7pm
Screening: 730pm
RSVP: Free or strongly encourage guaranteed $20 two-drink included RSVP.
Address: Industry City Bandshell Stage, Courtyard 1/2 at Industry City in Brooklyn, New York between 36th and 37th street and 2nd and 3rd Avenues.
ENTER 238 36th Street, Brooklyn, NY on your GPS device
The selection of music documentaries was curated by audience vote from our summer concert series and the horror movies came from out of our brains!
Seating for these screenings are limited to 150 people or so (with slightly more for the music docs so peeps can throw down appropriately.
Fans who purchase the 2 drink guaranteed RSVP will be guaranteed entry, natch! So you will save money at the bar, AND make sure you aren’t shut out!
This event is free with RSVP, ages 8 and up are welcome. There will be drink specials, all night, as well.
Limited seating (about 100-125 seats), tons of standing room. No strollers.
No outside beverages. There will be drink specials all night long from our courtyard bar.
While we do our best to gauge the number of RSVPs, entry is still on a first-come, first-served basis, so please arrive early! Once we hit capacity, we will only let people in on an in and out basis! Fans who purchase the 2 drink RSVP at check-out will be guaranteed entry!
The venue is located in an open-air courtyard featuring a full concert sound stage. Fans can get affordable drinks from the venue’s bar and order food from over 17 options inside the adjoining food hall.
How to get here:
Take the D, N, R lines to 36th street station in Brooklyn and walk west one block to Industry City. 3 stops from Manhattan. 30 minutes from Herald Square.
From Long Island, take the LIRR to Atlantic Terminal then take the D, N or R train to 36th street.
